text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's Social policy ministry and a visiting International Monetary Fund (IMF) mission were expected to discuss today wages in the public sector in the second half of this year, when an IMF-prescribed restrictive monetary mechanism is to be introduced in the country. @

-- Bulgaria's Interior minister Bogomil Bonev said the ministry would file many lawsuits against local customs officers on charges of profiteering in a bid to tighten border control and boost revenue from customs duties and and excise fees.

-- Bulgaria had set a minimum price of $100.2 million for the sale of 57 percent of the state fertiliser producer Chimko Vratsa, Privatisation Agency's executive director Alexander Sabotinov said. The deadline for submitting bids for the stake in Chimko is set on July 9 .

-- Bulgaria and Hungary had agreed to abolish customs duties on all goods by the year 2001 as part of Bulgaria's bid to join the Central European Free Trade Association (CEFTA), a Bulgarian trade ministry official said.
-- Bulgaria's state cigarette maker Blagoevgrad BT said it had posted 2.4 billion lev net profit for 1996.
-- Bulgaria's trade turnover with Japan last year amounted to $57 million, down from $80 million in 1992 and $200 million in 1988, Bulgaria's deputy trade minister Minko Gerdzhikov said. @

-- Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency said it had set a deadline until early June for submitting bids for 55 percent stake in the Sofia Grand Hotel in Sofia by potential investors, the hotel's executive director Stilian Stoichev said.
Last year the Agency approved the Bulgarian company G & B Travel as a buyer but the company declined to complete the deal because of the uncertainty of the local banking system. @

-- Bulgaria's National Security Service has received information that some criminal groupings were planning to obstruct the introduction of a currency board system in the country, Interior minister Bogomil Bonev said in an interview with the national radio.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet is expected to discuss today raising minimum pensions to 27,000 levs from 24,000 levs from July 1.

-- The wholesale price of pork in Bulgaria is expected to rise three-fold to around 12,000 levs per kilogramme because of high prices of fodder grain from this year's harvest, local agriculture experts said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
